- Digital Signatures
- Zone Signing

##### On DNS Manager:
check if zone replicates on all DNS servers on the domain:
![20250116104845.png](20250116104845.png)

##### Steps 
![](data:image/png;base64,)

Select Customize zone signing parameters , and go with defaults, 

Add new key for record 

![20250116105104.png](20250116105104.png)

Add new key for zone with 2048 length
 ![20250116105436.png](20250116105436.png)
but  Sure you select Enable the distribution of trust anchors for this zone
![20250116105547.png](20250116105547.png)


check if the dnssec is enabled with dnscmd:
```powershell
dnscmd /info /enablednssec
```

![20250317133912.png](20250317133912.png)
![20250521120231.png](20250521120231.png)

Check on all DCs:
```powershell
# Get all domain controllers in the domain  
$domainControllers = Get-ADDomainController -Filter * | Select-Object -ExpandProperty HostName
# Loop through each domain controller and check EnableDnsSec  
$results = foreach ($dc in $domainControllers) {  
    try {  
        $dnsSetting = Get-DnsServerSetting -ComputerName $dc -ErrorAction Stop  
        [PSCustomObject]@{  
            DomainController = $dc  
            EnableDnsSec     = $dnsSetting.EnableDnsSec  
            Status           = "Success"  
        }  
    } catch {  
        [PSCustomObject]@{  
            DomainController = $dc  
            EnableDnsSec     = "N/A"  
            Status           = "Error: $($_.Exception.Message)"  
        }  
    }  
}
# Display the results  
$results | Format-Table -AutoSize
```

![20250526145013.png](20250526145013.png)


In the previous example, DNSSEC validation is disabled. To enable DNSSEC validation, you must configure the value to 1. Then Restart DNS service and clear cash.
```powershell
dnscmd /config /enablednssec 1
```

![20250317134000.png](20250317134000.png)



![20250521120150.png](20250521120150.png)

![20250521115717.png](20250521115717.png)


##### Test
To test
```powershell
#run on your pc
Resolve-DnsName -server DC01.contoso.com -Dnsonly -DnssecOk
#Replicate all DCs
repadmin /syncall /ADep

```

![20250116110013.png](20250116110013.png)
##### Force Clients to use DNSSEC:

Create new GPO  : Computer Configuration > Policies > Windows Settings >  Name Resolution Policy

Add Zone name on Suffix and select Enable DNSSEC in this rule & require DNS client to check that name and address has been validated by the DNS server .

Then click on Create to create the rule.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Link the GPO to Domain OU

![20250116110822.png](20250116110822.png)


Check policy on client:
run powershell as admin:
```powershell
#test gpo dnssec
gpupdate /force
Get-DnsClientNrptPolicy
```

![20250116111026.png](20250116111026.png)

netsh namespace show policy

##### Child domain scenario 
if there is a child domain and another child zone then it should be signed also. then import its key to the parent zone.
locate the DS file on the child zone then move it to the parent and import it

```powershell
Import-DnsServerResourceRecordDS -ZoneName lab.local -DSSetFile "c:\windows\system32\dns\dsset-child.lab.local"
```
you can confirm with 
```powershell
Get-DnsServerResourceRecord -ZoneName lab.local -RRType DS
```

![20250317134402.png](20250317134402.png)

##### Troubleshooting:


[DNSSEC Trust Points missing from DNS manager on Server 2016 – "Bytes of helpful information"](https://www.johndball.com/dnssec-trust-points-missing-from-dns-manager-on-server-2016/)


[Trust Anchors | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/windows/it-pro/windows-server-2012-R2-and-2012/dn593672\(v=ws.11\)#the-delegation-signer-ds-resource-record)

To verify zone signing in Windows PowerShell

```powershell
Get-DnsServerZone -Name lab.local
```
Verify that **True** is displayed in the **IsSigned** column.

```powershell
Get-DnsServerResourceRecord -ZoneName lab.local
```
Verify that RRSIG, DNSKEY, and NSEC resource records are present in the zone.
![20250317135001.png](20250317135001.png)
[Procedure: Verify Zone Signing | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/windows/it-pro/windows-server-2012-r2-and-2012/dn593691\(v=ws.11\)#to-verify-zone-signing-in-windows-powershell)

To verify trust anchors:
```powershell
get-dnsservertrustanchor lab.local

OR
resolve-dnsname –name lab.local.trustanchors –type dnskey –server dns1
```
[Step-by-Step: Demonstrate DNSSEC in a Test Lab | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/windows/it-pro/windows-server-2012-R2-and-2012/hh831411\(v=ws.11\)#to-verify-trust-anchors)

Delete and re-distribute trust anchors using Windows PowerShell
```powershell
remove-dnsservertrustanchor –name lab.local
```

then Verify that “Failed to enumerate the trust anchors” is displayed.
```powershell
get-dnsservertrustanchor lab.local
```

```powershell
 remove-dnsserverzone –name trustanchors
```

add the keys again
```powershell
get-dnsserverresourcerecord –zonename lab.local –rrtype dnskey –computername dc1 | %{ $_.recorddata | add-dnsservertrustanchor -name lab.local }
```

[Step-by-Step: Demonstrate DNSSEC in a Test Lab | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/windows/it-pro/windows-server-2012-R2-and-2012/hh831411\(v=ws.11\)#delete-and-re-distribute-trust-anchors-using-windows-powershell)


To test:

Enable on all DCs:
```powershell
# Get all domain controllers in the domain
$domainControllers = Get-ADDomainController -Filter * | Select-Object -ExpandProperty HostName
# Ensure output directory exists
$directoryPath = "C:\_GB"
if (-not (Test-Path $directoryPath)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $directoryPath | Out-Null }
$timestamp = Get-Date -Format "yyyyMMdd_HHmmss"
# Save status before changes
$beforeChangePath = "$directoryPath\DNSSECEnabled_Before_$timestamp.csv"
$beforeChangeResults = $domainControllers | ForEach-Object {
$dnsSetting = Get-DnsServerSetting -ComputerName $_ -ErrorAction Stop
    [PSCustomObject]@{
        DomainController = $_
        EnableDnsSec  = if ($dnsSetting -and $dnsSetting.EnableDnsSec -ne $null) { $dnsSetting.EnableDnsSec -join "," } else { "N/A" }
        Status = if ($dnsSetting) { "Success" } else { "Error" }
    }
}
$beforeChangeResults | Export-Csv -Path $beforeChangePath -NoTypeInformation
# Apply changes and save status after changes
$afterChangePath = "$directoryPath\DNSSECEnabled_After_$timestamp.csv"
$afterChangeResults = $domainControllers | ForEach-Object {
    $dnsSetting = Get-DnsServerSetting -ComputerName $_ -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    $dnsSecStatus = if ($dnsSetting -and -not $dnsSetting.EnableDnsSec) {
Invoke-Command -ComputerName $_ -ScriptBlock {
    dnscmd /config /enablednssec 1
} -ErrorAction Stop
            "Enabled"
        } elseif ($dnsSetting -and $dnsSetting.EnableDnsSec -ne $null) {
            $dnsSetting.EnableDnsSec -join ","
        } else {
            "N/A"
    }
    [PSCustomObject]@{
        DomainController = $_
        EnableDnsSec  = $dnsSecStatus
        Status = if ($dnsSetting) { "Success" } else { "Error" }
    }
}
$afterChangeResults | Export-Csv -Path $afterChangePath -NoTypeInformation
```
